ribbon_weight_disclosure.purpose: Answers the orchestrator's explicit ask: report plainly what F1-amp does to ribbon weight/width per law, and state whether it forecloses Jay's open decision 10 (thinner-style-A vs pre-fix-weight-B).
ribbon_weight_disclosure.finding: F1-amp is NOT ink-neutral and does NOT uniformly increase ink. Three of four laws (interlockWeave, trochoidLoop, onePenDown) lose fill ink (-1.0% to -5.4%); only amplitudeOnly gains (+1.5% to +2.4%). All four stay comfortably inside the +-8% bound. onePenDown -- already flagged by F1-erode-plan section 7 as reading visibly thinner after F1-placement -- loses the MOST ink of the four under F1-amp (-5.37% fill ink). THIS DOES NOT FORECLOSE DECISION 10 in either direction, but it is directionally relevant: F1-amp makes onePenDown (and interlockWeave/trochoidLoop) read LIGHTER, not bolder. If Jay answers decision 10 with 'restore the pre-fix boldness (style B)', the lever remains the weight field, exactly as F1-erode-plan section 7 already said -- F1-amp's amplitude floor is not that lever and does not substitute for it. Mechanism: amplitude increases arc length (elongation), which by itself would ADD ink, but the erosion/self-occlusion/off-surface-rejection pipeline downstream evidently removes more than that adds for 3 of 4 laws at this specific density -- a genuine, measured, non-obvious net effect, not a simple 'more waviness = more ink' story.
